purpose: External eval set for vibe-requirements-spec. Prompts live outside skills/ so they are not bundled as skill content. Covers artifact-by-default requirements drafting before implementation planning, explicit chat-only/no-file operation, the three requirement modes, docs/specs default paths, same-spec replacement revision, requirements lifecycle evidence outside the artifact, environment-variable documented-contract behavior, document language selection, factual-error handling, destructive-change confirmation, downstream-workflow neutrality, non-technical communication, scope boundaries, defaults versus decisions, write-safety, auditability, contradiction handling, and stop behavior after finish or handoff wording. Environment-variable cases are prompt-embedded documented-contract coverage because the shared runner does not provide per-eval environment injection.
common_assertions: When artifact mode applies, output records a Markdown requirements spec at a concrete repository-relative location and returns a concise chat summary with that location, requirements-finished or next-phase handoff evidence when available, blockers or unknowns, and exact next user action; when explicit chat-only, lifecycle-summary, or no-write fallback mode applies, output states that the saved spec was not altered when applicable and gives the exact next action to create, update, finish, or hand off the spec.

While the skill is active, output does not create implementation plans, implementation task entries, code changes, tests, verification command lists, commits, release work, changelog edits, or unrelated files.

Output does not blend confirmed requirements, proposed defaults, ideas or options, user decisions, assumptions, out-of-scope items, acceptance criteria, evidence, and open risks or unknowns into a single recommendation; when artifact mode or a structured requirements summary is in scope, those categories are separated explicitly.

When artifact mode applies, generated spec artifact headings and generated prose use the selected document language resolved from explicit artifact-language request, documented environment contract, or skill default, while useful user-authored original wording, product names, domain terms, identifiers, paths, commands, and quoted text are preserved.

When artifact mode applies, the spec artifact includes `Requirement mode` in `Spec metadata` and includes an `Evidence and constraints` section that records decision-affecting local paths, external sources or URLs, and unverified facts without treating unsupported claims as confirmed.

When artifact mode applies, output does not write approval-status sections or fields into the spec artifact, including `Approval state`, `Status: Draft`, `Status: Awaiting explicit approval`, `Status: Approved`, `Status: Reopened after approval`, or `Approval note`, and does not write `Revision notes`, lifecycle status fields, or dated change-history entries.

Ambiguous positive replies such as `OK`, `looks good`, `ready`, `continue`, or `go ahead` are not treated as requirements-finished evidence unless they clearly finish the current requirements or unambiguously ask for a next phase from the current spec.
If the conversation or artifact already identifies a spec path, output updates or preserves that same spec instead of creating a new unrelated spec.
Output does not require, name, or route to a specific downstream skill or workflow; it may refer generically to a later implementation-planning phase after requirements are finished.
If output includes `Can default`, defaults do not select or pre-stage behavior for unselected adjacent surfaces with conditional wording such as `within whichever ... you select`.
When creative exploration is useful, output presents brainstormed ideas as candidate options with tradeoffs and does not treat unchosen ideas as confirmed requirements.
Output marks inferred behavior as an assumption or proposed default, not as a confirmed user requirement.
Output keeps adjacent features out of scope unless the user explicitly includes them in the first useful slice.

Output does not put unconfirmed adjacent capabilities in confirmed requirements with a `subject to confirmation` qualifier; they stay in out-of-scope items, decisions needed, or candidate options until selected.
Output uses the user's language for the chat-facing summary while preserving code identifiers, paths, commands, API names, locale tags, environment variables, and product terms.

evals.name: Strict mode for vague profile UI
evals.prompt: I want users to be able to edit their display name on the profile screen, but I have not decided the details yet. Make it feel right.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates an English Markdown requirements spec under docs/specs, selects strict-four-choice, asks one visible requirements decision question with four or three choices, includes one mildly challenging option with risk and adoption conditions, and stops without planning implementation.
expectations: A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path; a claim in `response.md` or an inline fenced draft alone is not enough.
Records `Requirement mode: strict-four-choice` in the spec metadata.
Includes `Evidence and constraints` and marks unsupported UI or validation facts as assumptions or unverified instead of confirmed.
Keeps the first scope limited to display-name editing.
Asks exactly one visible requirements decision question in the active response; a separate startup subagent-permission question does not count as a requirements decision question.
Presents three or four labeled options, and each option states the requirement that would be adopted plus benefits, drawbacks, and risks or assumptions.
Includes one mildly challenging option with explicit risk, assumptions, and adoption conditions.
Does not plan code edits, tests, files other than the spec, or commits.

expectations: Treats the request as artifact-mode requirements drafting, not chat-only exploration, because the user did not explicitly ask for no file.
A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path.
Records `Requirement mode: strict-four-choice` in the spec metadata.
Uses a grouped confirmation checklist or equivalent grouped decisions in the spec rather than many direct questions in the active response.
Asks exactly one visible high-impact question in the active response.
Recommends a bounded first useful scope that does not include admin screens or delivery logs unless the user explicitly selects them.
Explains SMS and push uncertainty in product terms such as cost, permission, provider setup, opt-in behavior, or compliance without inventing provider facts.
Keeps admin screens and delivery logs out of confirmed requirements, first-slice defaults, and acceptance criteria unless the user explicitly selects them.
Names unresolved channel and behavior decisions as blockers to finishing requirements or later planning.
Does not name or require a specific downstream workflow.

Explicitly treats `somehow create contacts` as an unresolved data contract, not a confirmed mapping, persistence, or duplicate-handling rule.

evals.expected_output: The agent creates or updates a requirements spec that surfaces the contradiction between migration, unchanged old reports, no compatibility code, and invisible behavior, then stops for user decisions.
expectations: A recorded non-response requirements spec artifact is produced at an explicit `docs/specs/` path.
Identifies the contradiction instead of smoothing it into a confident requirement.
Separates possible interpretations such as copy-on-read, one-time migration, dual reader, or no migration.
Explains the consequence of each choice in user or data-safety terms.
Marks data compatibility and rollback or recovery expectations as blocking decisions or blocking unknowns.
Does not propose implementation details as if the contradiction were resolved.
Keeps drafting active until the migration contract is chosen and requirements-finished evidence is available.

scoring.notes: These evals focus on observable requirements-spec behavior rather than subjective writing quality. They pressure artifact-by-default drafting, explicit chat-only/no-file operation, strict/lightweight/freestyle modes, docs/specs default paths, same-spec continuity for historical specs/ paths, requirements lifecycle evidence outside artifacts, environment-variable documented-contract handling, document language selection, no approval-status fields, no implementation while active, factual-error correction, destructive-risk confirmation, downstream-workflow neutrality, scope separation, write-safety, auditability, and stop behavior after finish or handoff wording. Environment-variable cases are not runtime subprocess environment proof because the current shared runner does not support per-eval env injection.
